newsitem.title: JAPAN: ADNOC OFFERS TERM NAPHTHA AT $22 PREMIUM - TRADERS.
newsitem.headline: ADNOC OFFERS TERM NAPHTHA AT $22 PREMIUM - TRADERS.

text.p: Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) has notified Japanese term naphtha lifters of its offer price of about $22 a tonne over the ADNOC formula for one-year supply contracts starting in September, traders here said on Friday.
The initial offer price compares with a $7.15 premium for the current term year.

The ADNOC offer price would be "prohibitive" for the potential buyers--one Japanese oil firm and a Japanese trading arm of a European major--partly because of recent declines of olefine and polyolefine prices in Asia, traders said.

Most polyethylene and polypropylene grades, both derived from naphtha, have fallen by $50 to $100 tonne a tonne, or 6 to 12 percent, in the past month on a C&F (cost and freight) Hong Kong basis due to sluggish regional demand.
The buyers are likely to aim for prices lower than the latest ADNOC premium of $21 a tonne, which was set for annual term supply contracts that started in July 1997, they said.
The two firms are expected to each import about 100,000 tonnes from ADNOC in the new term year, they added.
Term naphtha premiums for Middle Eastern cargoes have shot up since last year amid expectations of growing naphtha demand in Asia with new petrochemical plants springing up across the region.

For instance, term prices for Saudi Arabia's A-180 naphtha, ethylene-rich paraffinic material favoured among petrochemical manufacturers, rose from $3.40 over the Aramco formula for the second half of 1996 to $6.50 for the first half of 1997.
The premium then revised up to $17.00 for the July-December loading.
